How casimir works

Source: vignettes/casimir-00-how-it-works.Rmd
casimir-00-how-it-works.Rmd

This guide describes the simulated fishery, the survey design, the estimators and the planted artefacts. The app’s Guide tab has a plain-language version. For worked examples see vignette("casimir-02-user-guide") and vignette("casimir-03-teaching").

1. What casimir does

casimir (Catch Sampling Inference Methods in R) simulates a small-scale fishery whose true landings are known, and the landing-site surveys that try to estimate them. It is built for training in catch assessment surveys: trainees design a stratified multi-stage survey, roll a sample, raise it to catch per species with the estimators of the FAO training, and spin the design many times to see its bias, precision and cost, for catch by species and for effort (landings, i.e. fishing trips).

A casimir run has seven layers, each a plain R function:

# Layer Function Object
1 Island (fishery) cas_fishery(island_x()) cas_fishery
2 Frame survey frame_survey() cas_frame
3 Design cas_design() cas_design
4 Roll (sample) draw_sample() cas_sample (forms A-C)
5 Raise (estimate) estimate_catch() cas_estimate
6 Series (survey years) run_survey(), catch_by(), effort_by() cas_survey
7 Spin (evaluate) replicate_design(), compare_designs(); over the years spin_series() cas_eval, cas_spins
- Truth cas_truth(), cas_effort_truth(), check_estimate(), planted_artefacts() answer key
- Cash out export_survey(), spins_long() csv files, long table

Seeds are derived per stream with seed_for(seed, tag), so a new sample does not change the fishery, and designs compared on the same fishery share the same random draws where they overlap.

2. The island: landing sites, segments and ranges

The fishery comes from the logbook simulator of cpueTargeting (simulate_logbook()): ten demersal and pelagic species on a shelf-to-slope grid with reef patches and a temperature gradient, Schaefer dynamics, and a fleet that chooses a tactic (reef handline, sediment longline, pelagic troll) and a cell by expected value. casimir switches on its optional landing layer (landing_settings()):

  • each boat has a home landing site on the coast, drawn by site type and segment (site_mix);
  • the weight of each cell in the choice of where to fish is multiplied by the segment’s reach from the home site, exp(-(d / range)^2);
  • each trip gets a fishing day (no fishing on Sundays, at most one trip per boat and day where possible) and a landing hour (departure + hours fished + travel).

island_x() sets up Island X of the FAO training concept by Pedro Barros (Data Collection and Estimation of Fisheries Quantities): nine sites of three types (Harbour, Beach, Jetty) and three segments.

Segment Boats Range Home tactics Based at
canoe 150 5 cells (12.5 km) Reef beaches, jetties
small_motor 60 12 cells (30 km) Reef, Sediment all site types
large_motor 15 25 cells (62.5 km) Pelagic, Sediment harbours, some jetties

The simulation runs for ten years and the survey programme covers the last five; the earlier years let stocks respond to fishing and the fleet change. Fishing pressure is moderate (catchability q = 0.004; the valuable reef species Dentex dentex, most exposed to the canoes, at 30% of the default catchability), so stocks decline without collapsing.

Boats join and leave the fleet over the whole period (island_x(entry = 0.4, exit = 0.1): 40% of the boats join after year 1, 10% leave), and trips per year grow with the number of active boats. The fleet grows by about half over ten years, so a frame survey that is not repeated goes out of date. fish$landings holds every trip with its site, date, segment and true landed weight by species: the census the survey estimates.

3. Frame survey and design

frame_survey() lists boats by site and segment (active in a reference year) and fishing days by quarter. The PSU is a landing site on a fishing day; strata are site type x quarter, and each visit records all segments, so each segment is raised in its own stratum (site type x quarter x segment).

cas_design() sets the stages:

Stage Unit Setting Recorded on
1 site-day m per site type and quarter; psu_select = "srs" or "systematic" Form A: N, landings counted by segment
2 landing n per segment and visit (all if fewer land) Form B: W, landed kg; hours fished
3 subsample w_kg per landing, in baskets of unit_kg Form C: species weights w_s

The subsample is drawn as w_kg / unit_kg baskets, each filled with the species mix of the landing (multinomial), so small subsamples miss rare species. design_cost() counts enumerator-hours per visit, landing and kg.

4. Estimators

estimate_catch() raises one stage at a time:

Step 1  landing   W_ijs = w_ijs / sum_s(w_ijs) * W_ij
Step 2  site-day  W_is  = N_i / n_i * sum_j W_ijs
Step 3  stratum   W_hs  = M_h / m_h * sum_i W_is
Step 4  total     W_s   = sum_h W_hs

Site-days with no landings of a segment count, with a catch of zero. The variance of step 3 is the ultimate-cluster estimator with the stage-1 finite population correction,

V(W_hs) = M_h^2 (1 - m_h / M_h) s^2_h / m_h

where s^2_h is the variance of the site-day totals; the second-stage term M_h / m_h sum_i N_i^2 (1 - n_i / N_i) s^2_i / n_i is returned as var_within. A census (all site-days, all landings, whole landings) recovers the true catch exactly, and over replicates the estimator is unbiased (tests in tests/testthat).

The CPUE x effort route (route = "effort") multiplies the mean catch per landing in the stratum by frame boats x fishing days x boat activity (landings counted per frame boat on the visited days). It agrees with the PSU route on average when the frame is up to date.

5. Catch by segment and the five-year programme

catch_by(estimate, by = "segment") sums the stratum estimates by species and segment (or site type, or quarter), with variances added over strata. run_survey() rolls and raises the same design in each survey year (by default the last five of the ten simulated years); frame = "first" keeps the frame survey of the first year throughout, so it ages as boats enter and leave. plot_series() shows the estimates with intervals against the truth.

Effort, the number of landings (fishing trips), is estimated alongside the catch: M_h / m_h * sum_i N_i from the landings counted on Form A, or frame boats x days x activity on the CPUE x effort route. effort_by() and plot_effort_series() compare it with the census (cas_effort_truth()).

spin_series() repeats the whole programme R times; summary_spins() and plot_spin_series() (a band of the middle 95% of the estimates, or paired bars) show the spread year by year against the truth, and spins_long() returns every estimate with its truth as one long table (iter, year, quarter, site type, segment, species).

On Island X boats join the fleet over the years (island_x(entry, exit)) and trips grow with the number of boats, so an old frame survey underestimates effort and catch more each year.

6. Planted artefacts

artefacts() switches on field problems; planted_artefacts() lists them for the answer key.

Artefact Setting Effect
High roller high_roller = 0-1 landings chosen with probability proportional to W^(3 * high_roller): catch biased up
Short watch short_watch = hour later landings neither counted nor sampled: long-range segments and their species biased down
Easy sites easy_sites = c(...) only these sites visited, M counts all: biased if their grounds differ
Dropped zeros dropped_zeros = TRUE visits with no landings not recorded: catch biased up
Top of the box top_of_box = 0-1 subsample favours valuable species: species split biased
Old frame old_frame = years frame boats out of date: CPUE x effort route biased

7. Spin: bias, CV and coverage

replicate_design() repeats Roll and Raise R times on the same island and compares the totals with the truth: relative bias (the house edge), CV, coverage of the 95% intervals and RMSE. compare_designs() does this for several designs, and days_vs_boats() builds designs of about equal cost that trade site-days for landings per visit.

spin_series() spins the whole programme: every replicate rolls and raises the design in each survey year. summary_spins() gives, per year, the mean and the middle 95% of the estimates against the truth, with bias and coverage; plot_spin_series() draws them as a band or as paired bars, for catch by species or effort by segment. spins_long() returns every estimate with its truth as one long table (iter, year, quarter, site type, segment, species), ready for csv or rds.

Coverage below 0.95 is expected for species whose catches are skewed (a few large landings) when strata have few site-days: the normal interval is too narrow. It is a teaching point, not an error.
